content.text:
The storage settings page now serves two audiences: admins get project-wide usage stats on top of the existing configuration view, and regular users get a page showing just their own space.

**What an admin sees** — a new "Usage" card between the health card and the configuration card, containing three KPI cards (Files, Size occupied, Users with files) and two bar charts side by side: size occupied by user, and files by user.

**What a regular user sees** — a "Your space" card with two KPI cards, Files and Size occupied, plus an intro that explains what the space is. They never see the backend configuration, bucket names, or credentials, because `getConfig` and `getHealth` remain admin-only procedures and the page only queries them for admins.

The numbers come from a new `storage.getUsage` procedure on `projectProtectedProcedure`. It always computes the caller's own space, and only attaches the per-user breakdown when `userRole === 'admin'`, so a non-admin cannot read other people's figures even by calling the endpoint directly. The aggregation lives in a new `apps/backend/src/services/storage/usage.ts` that walks the storage keys: `getScopeUsage` sums one user's space, and `getProjectUsageByUser` groups a whole project by owner, sorted heaviest first. Both return zeros when permanent storage is disabled rather than throwing. Two new key helpers back this — `projectRoot` for the project-wide prefix and `userIdFromKey` to recover the owner from a key.

The breakdown is scoped to the current project, not the whole instance, since "admin" in nao is a project-level role. Owner names come from the project's member list; a space whose owner has since left the project falls back to its user id rather than a shared "unknown" label, so those bars stay distinct.

Three things had to open up to let non-admins reach the page at all: the route guard moved from `requireAdminNonCloud` to a new `requireNonViewerNonCloud`, the sidebar entry now shows for any non-viewer, and I added a non-admin "Storage Usage" entry to the settings search index (the existing configuration and health entries stay `adminOnly`). Viewers are still excluded, matching how the codebase treats them elsewhere — they can't send messages, so they have no files.

Verification: `npm run lint` and `npm run format:check` are clean, and I added `storage-usage.test.ts` plus cases in `storage-keys.test.ts` covering cross-user and cross-project isolation and the storage-disabled path — 65 tests pass across the storage suites. The 5 failures you'll see in `storage-tools.test.ts` are pre-existing (a missing ripgrep binary); I confirmed they fail identically on a clean tree.

One judgement call worth flagging: KPI sizes use the existing `formatBytes` helper (binary, "4.3 MB"), while the bar chart's y-axis ticks use the codebase's d3 convention for bytes (SI, `.2s` + "B"), with `formatBytes` in the tooltip. Axis ticks can therefore read a few percent differently from the KPI. Happy to force one convention if that bothers you.
